headline: Sales grow on FX and acquisitions as margins compress
summary_short: AptarGroup's Q2 FY2026 net sales rose 6.3% y/y to $1,026.5M on FX tailwinds and acquisitions, but net income fell 21.6% y/y to $87.6M ($1.36 diluted EPS) as a lower-margin Pharma mix and higher costs compressed operating margin to 12.3% of sales.
summary_long: Net sales grew 6.3% y/y to $1,026.5M: a weaker dollar added 2%, acquisitions added 3%, and core (organic) sales rose just 1% as Closures volume strength and cost pass-through offset lower tooling sales. Cost of sales rose to 64.4% of sales from 62.0% on a lower-margin Pharma mix (fewer emergency-medicine sales) and higher input/operating costs, while D&A rose on growth capex and acquisitions. Operating income fell 12.2% y/y to $126.7M; interest expense rose $5.2M on higher-rate refinancing debt, and the effective tax rate rose to 23.5% from 20.0%, pulling net income down 21.6% to $87.6M. Aptar guided Q3 2026 adjusted EPS to $1.45-$1.53 and FY2026 capex to $260-$280M.

H1 2026 operating cash flow of $222.2M and revolver draws outweighed $123.0M of capex and $150.0M of buybacks, lifting cash versus a year earlier despite a sequential decline.
Treasury stock rose to $1,097.0M from $740.0M a year earlier on $150.0M of H1 2026 buybacks, outweighing retained-earnings growth from net income.
Reflects $150.0M of H1 2026 share buybacks reducing the diluted count from 67.0M to 64.2M, only partly offset by new stock-award issuance.

Management attributed sales growth mainly to currency and acquisitions with only 1% core growth; Pharma's lower-margin mix and higher costs drove the y/y profit decline. Aptar guided Q3 2026 adjusted EPS to $1.45-$1.53.
